removal.effect: Removes the tool from the prompt entirely.
removal.note: This is one of Claude Code's OWN tools. Removing it does not degrade the agent gracefully — it takes away a capability the model is expected to have, and anything that depended on it fails. The token saving is real and it is almost never worth it.

removal.effect: Hides the skill from the listing, so its entry stops being sent.
removal.note: Denying a skill with `Skill(skill-1)` instead would NOT save anything — a scoped rule blocks the call but leaves the entry in the prompt. Deleting `~/.claude/skills/skill-1/` also works and is permanent. If you want to KEEP this skill and still stop paying for most of it, set it to "name-only" instead of "off": that lists the name without the description, which is nearly all of the weight. "user-invocable-only" hides it from the model while leaving /skill-1 working for you.

removal.effect: The command removes the whole `beta` server and every tool it declares. The settings fragment removes just this one tool and keeps the rest.
removal.note: `claude mcp remove` takes an optional `-s local|user|project`; with no scope it removes the server from whichever scope it is defined in. There is no `claude mcp disable` — to keep the config and turn the server off, use the `/mcp` panel.
